flags.kv_pool_note: --max-total-tokens can only LOWER the profiled pool; the actual size is in flags.resolved.max_total_num_tokens when the log reports it

sharing.definition: block_sharing_rate = leading block-aligned prefix blocks already present in an earlier request / total block-aligned prompt blocks. This is the infinite-cache ORACLE hit rate and an upper bound on any measured one.

notes: CLOSED LOOP: N workers, each sends its next request when the previous one finishes, so exactly N are in flight. Latency is timed from the moment the worker became free; coordinated omission does not apply because there is no schedule to fall behind, and no queue deeper than N can form by construction. This mode cannot locate a saturation knee (that is W2's job).

definitions.preemptions: delta sglang:num_retracted_requests_total; absent series on a live endpoint (sglang:num_running_reqs present) = 0 (labeled counter, exported after first increment)
definitions.evictions: delta sglang:evicted_tokens_total (TOKENS, not blocks); absent series on a live endpoint = 0, as for preemptions
definitions.prefix_hit_rate: delta sglang:prefill_effective_tokens_total with mode in ['device_hit', 'host_hit', 'storage_hit'] / delta sglang:prefill_effective_tokens_total over all modes (TOKEN granularity). sglang:cache_hit_rate is NOT used: it covers the last prefill batch only
